transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-02-03
Start: 09:00 UTC | Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Nina (Redwood CSM) -- Priya (Asteron), Mark (CTO), Jamal (Security), Tara (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Goal: align on adoption runway, SLA requirements, cost tradeoffs, and pilot scope for Dedicated/private deployment.
- Key asks: security posture (KMS/HSM), audit logs, SSO, data residency; headroom for burst capacity; quantization and batching guidance to lower cost.
- Agreed next steps: share pricing, run benchmarks, secure security docs, schedule architecture deep-dive.

Topics covered:
1) Current usage and projected uptake
2) Recent incidents / reliability concerns and SLA targets
3) Dedicated vs hosted vs private tradeoffs (latency/cost/security)
4) Pilot scope, benchmarks and rollout timeline
5) Security/compliance checklist and integrations

Action items (auto-list): see metadata action_items above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll keep this tight, 45ish to 60, uh 54 minutes on the calendar. quick intro — i'm samira, account lead. liam, nina are with me from redwood.
[00:12] Priya: thanks. yes, we wanted to go through current metrics and make sure we have a plan for the pilot and the SLA asks. we're starting to see user uptake after beta.
[00:25] Liam: great. can you share a bit about current traffic profile — average token size, p95 latency tolerated, and what percent of calls are chat vs completion?
[00:36] Priya: sure. right now it's about 120k requests/day, average prompt ~= 420 tokens in, 130 tokens out. p95 latency target from product is 350 ms, but the web UI tolerates up to 500ms for non-critical flows. about 70% chat-style sessions, 30% single-shot generation.
[00:58] Mark: to add, our monthly token volume sits at roughly 15M tokens, and dev forecast says 2.5x growth over next quarter if adoption continues. cost is a hard stop for finance — we need a predictable runway.
[01:12] Samira: understood. thats where dedicated capacity or commitment can really help — predictable throughput and unit economics. liam, quick note on batching strategies?
[01:23] Liam: yeah, so for that mix we typically recommend continuous batching with a low-latency cutoff; also prefix caching for common system prompts. we can suggest quantization profile — 8-bit mixed quant for most workloads keeps quality similar but drops GPU memory and cost.
[01:38] Tara: curious, how destructive is quantization to our finance queries? we've seen hallucinations when we tried 4-bit on another stack.
[01:46] Liam: 4-bit is riskier, especially for math/long context. 8-bit mixed quant keeps attention kernels intact and usually safe. we do test suites; we'll include the regression evals in the benchmark.
[01:58] Jamal: security first stuff — we need SOC 2 type II evidence, encryption with our KMS (we use Azure Key Vault), SAML SSO, RBAC controls, and audit logs for token-level access. can we get a doc with specifics?
[02:14] Nina: yes. we'll circulate the security pack. redwood private supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM, SSO via SAML, and per-route RBAC. the docs will have the api endpoints for audit logs, retention options.
[02:31] Priya: good. also data residency — some PII flows must stay in eu-west region. do you support region pinning for private/dedicated?
[02:41] Samira: yes, region pinning is supported for both Dedicated and Private modes. hosted API can be region limited but dedicated gives stronger guarantees.
[02:48] Mark: what about fallbacks? if capacity spikes, will requests fail or auto-failover to a smaller model?
[02:56] Liam: we have smart routing and fallback policies. you can set fail-open to a compatible model variant (lower-cost) or queue/burst to a higher tier if committed capacity allows. we'll demo this in the architecture review.
[03:10] Priya: perfect, because we cannot have user-visible errors during peak.
[03:15] Samira: quick question on incidents — you mentioned a couple of flakiness reports last month, can you walk us through?
[03:22] Tara: yes, two incidents. one was an autoscaler mis-config where burst policy wasn't applied; another was transient GPU OOM in a multi-tenant spot pool. both were short but hit the checkout pipeline.
[03:33] Liam: understandable. for Dedicated we'd recommend isolated GPU pools, configured autoscaling policies with headroom — plus KV cache warmup to avoid OOMs at rollout. sounds like you want guaranteed p99 SLOs?
[03:45] Mark: p99 800ms and p95 350ms target. for some flows we want p99 lower but open to discussion.
[03:53] Liu* (transcript artifact): [brief crosstalk]...
[03:57] Samira: noted: p95 350ms, p99 target 800ms as baseline for pilot. we'll annotate the SLA matrix.
[04:05] Priya: on cost — can you show projected numbers for hosted vs dedicated with our 15M tokens/month baseline?
[04:13] Samira: i'll send the model-level cost run. rough math: hosted best-case about $X0k/mo, dedicated reserved node (8xA100 equiv) with 20% commit looks like $Yk/mo but gets you stable latency and seat for burst. we'll send exact numbers in the sheet.
[04:29] Mark: finance will need a spread of commit vs on-demand and forecast scenarios.
[04:34] Samira: absolutely, that's in the next steps.
[04:39] Jamal: second security topic: audit logs — we need token-level hashing and a way to scrub PII before logs are persisted. is there a scrub layer?
[04:50] Nina: we offer pre-ingestion redaction hooks and prefix/KV masking. also configurable retention TTLs for logs in the control plane. for Private deployments you can host logs in your VPC and tie them to your KMS.
[05:05] Priya: that works. for the pilot, we'd like on-prem-like assurances but without full on-prem cost; Dedicated in a VPC with customer-managed KMS might be the middle ground.
[05:16] Liam: exactly, Dedicated + VPC with KMS bridges that gap. we can also provide an on-prem package if you need air-gapped.
[05:26] Priya: timeline: we want pilot in prod-like traffic within 4 weeks. is that feasible?
[05:33] Samira: feasible if we get the benchmark dataset and keys this week and a 2-week sprint to deploy Dedicated pool and run acceptance tests. so yes, 3-4 weeks seems realistic.
[05:44] Mark: okay, acceptance criteria: a) p95 < 350ms, b) no PII persisted in logs, c) cost per 1k tokens within agreed band, d) regression evals pass for intent and hallucination thresholds.
[05:58] Liam: we'll codify those in the runbook and automate evals. also include sample prompts for the regression set.
[06:07] Tara: any gotchas on model rollouts? we have several model variants internally.
[06:12] Liam: rollout supported — canary, A/B, or immediate. can set automatic fallback if new model exceeds error or latency thresholds. we'll propose rollout policy for your use-case.
[06:23] Priya: about caching — what's typical savings for our prompt distribution?
[06:28] Liam: with prefix caching and session reuse, bench indicate 18-24% token savings for chat products with repeated system prompts; KV warm cache for repeated retrievals can get an additional 10%.
[06:39] Mark: good. on billing, we need token-level breakouts for embeddings vs generations. do you provide detailed billing reports?
[06:47] Nina: yes, the console provides token-level, route-level breakdowns and per-token cost. we can also export CSVs nightly.
[06:56] Jamal: competitor question — CloudEndpoint Co pitched lower latency at similar cost. why Redwood?
[07:02] Samira: quick answer: our value is predictable inference economics + unified tooling across hosted/dedicated/private. plus first-class evals and production routing controls. we'll share a short competitive matrix.
[07:16] Priya: ok great. what is needed from us this week?
[07:20] Samira: 1) pilot dataset + list of critical prompts 2) security must-haves doc (Jamal), 3) preferred pilot dates 4) sandbox API keys request.
[07:28] Priya: we'll get dataset and prompts by 2028-02-05. Jamal will push the compliance matrix.
[07:34] Jamal: yes by 2028-02-07.
[07:38] Samira: liam, can you run a quick note on benchmarks to upload?
[07:42] Liam: i'll upload the benchmark runbook, scripts, and a sample results sheet to the shared drive; we'll target a synthetic replay of 1k rps for 5 minutes with your distribution and a second run at burst.
[07:56] Priya: question on observability: can we get token-level traces and per-request latency breakdowns?
[08:03] Nina: yes — per-route dashboards, per-token histograms, and trace hooks. we can send a sample dashboard.
[08:12] Mark: one more: SLAs — where is the penalty or credit mechanics?
[08:17] Samira: SLA credits are in the enterprise contracts for Dedicated; we'll include a draft in the pricing doc.
[08:25] Priya: ok, good.
[08:28] Samira: recap: Samira sends pilot pricing + commit scenarios; liam sends benchmark runbook & scripts; nina opens onboarding ticket and dashboard samples; jamal shares compliance matrix; customer team to provide dataset and prompts. schedule deep-dive for private deployment architecture.
[08:46] Mark: agreed. can we have a short demo of failover policies in the deep-dive?
[08:50] Liam: yes, we'll script a small demo to show routing and fallback to a smaller model variant.
[08:57] Tara: thanks everyone.
[09:00] Samira: thanks all, we'll follow up in email and include next steps.

End of transcript.
